text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian actress, CARRIE MOORE, was born in 1882. She was
nicknamed "The Vital Spark". She played in "Robin Hood", "The
Merry Widow", "Tom Jones" and "A Little Bit of Fluff".
GEORGE 'GUBBY' ALLEN, who was the Australian-born captain of
the 1936/37 English cricket team, was born in 1902.
American economist MILTON FRIEDMAN, an advocate of the free
market economy, was born in 1912.

Australian world champion squash star, HEATHER MCKAY, was born in 1941 at Queanbeyan in New South Wales. She was described as the 'greatest female squash player in the world' and was never beaten in her professional career.

American singer, guitarist and songwriter, LOBO, was born in 1943. His hits included "Me And You And A Dog Named Boo" (1971), "I'd Love You To Want Me" (1972) and "Don't Expect Me To Be Your Friend" (1972).
American actress, GERALDINE CHAPLIN, the daughter of silent film comedian CHARLIE CHAPLIN, was born in 1944.
The British bass player with 'Herman's Hermits', KARL GREEN, was born in 1947.

Australian tennis star, EVONNE GOOLAGONG CAWLEY, was born in the New South Wales country town of Barellan in 1951. She began her career at the age of 11. She won 92 international championships, including four Australian Opens and two Wimbledon singles championships. She was ranked as one of the top four players in the world, and was the world's Number two seed before she retired.
British cellist with E.L.O. from 1971, HUGH MACDOWELL, was
born in 1953.
** EVENTS **
1886 : Famous pianist, Abbe FRANZ LISZT, died from
pneumonia.
1902 : An explosion at the Port Kembla colliery, near
Wollongong, killed 87 miners. Most of the dead were overcome by gas. The hero of the disaster was Major McCABE, who was killed by fumes while making his third rescue attempt.
1910 : Dr HAWLEY HARVEY CRIPPEN and his 27-year-old

mistress, ETHEL LE NEVE, were charged with the murder of CRIPPEN's wife, whose mutilated and dismembered body was found buried in the cellar of her London home. CRIPPEN and LE NEVE were discovered by the captain of the "SS Montrose" who had read a newspaper description of the wanted couple. The captain radioed Britain and a Scotland Yard inspector, disguised as a St Lawrence river pilot, boarded the "Montrose" and arrested the couple off the coast of Canada. CRIPPEN was convicted and executed.
1941 : HERMAN GOERING gave a written directive to police
chief REINHARD HEYDRICH to draft a plan for the elimination of European Jews, the "final solution".
1949 : Troops moved into nine New South Wales coal mines
as a coal strike continued into its fifth week. More than 250,000 coal miners resumed work two weeks later and the Emergency Act was repealed. The strike was over pay claims and improved conditions.
1964 : A Rolling Stones concert in Belfast was stopped
after only 12 minutes, because of rioting fans.
1964 : Country singer, JIM REEVES, died in a plane crash
in Tennessee. He was 40. His hits included "He'll Have To Go", "Welcome To My World" and "I Love You Because".
1965 : Television commercials for cigarettes were banned
in Britain.
1967 : Rolling Stones MIKE JAGGER and KEITH RICHARD went
free on appeal after having their prison terms on drug charges quashed.
1969 : The United States spacecraft "Mariner 6" sent back
close-up pictures of Mars.
1972 : The Box Flat coal mine on the West Moreton
coalfields at Ipswich near Brisbane was rocked by an explosion which killed 17 men. The mine was sealed for at least six months to suffocate the fierce underground fire. Bulldozers rammed
thousands of tonnes of earth and rock into the underground tunnel network, where 14 of the men were killed in the blast. More than 230 miners lost their jobs when the mine closed.
1975 : Irish pop group the 'Miami Showband' was ambushed
and murdered by Protestant gunmen in Northern Ireland.
1977 : The film "Storm Boy" premiered in Melbourne.
1978 : GOUGH WHITLAM resigned from parliament. He was

Labor Party leader from 1967 until 1978 and was prime minister from 1972 until 1975, when his government was sacked by the Governor-General and subsequently defeated in an election landslide to the Coalition.
1983 : JAN STEPHENSON became the first Australian to win
the U.S. Women's Open golf title.
1989 : Shi'ite Muslim extremists announced they had

murdered Colonel WILLIAM HIGGINS, the United States marine abducted in Lebanon 17 months earlier. The group, calling itself the 'Organisation for the Oppressed of the Earth', also released a video showing a bound and gagged man revolving slowly at the end of a rope. The CIA examined the tape and said it believed Colonel HIGGINS had been killed earlier.
1991 : At the end of a two-day summit, Presidents BUSH and
GORBACHEV signed the START treaty cutting their nuclear arsenals.
1994 : The Security Council authorised the use of force
in Haiti, clearing the way for a U.S.-led invasion of the country to restore exiled President JEAN-BERTRAND ARISTIDE to power.
1995 : In a move that took both Hollywood and Wall Street
by surprise, the Walt Disney Co. said it would pay $19 billion for Capital Cities/ABC Inc, creating a major force in the entertainment and media industry.
1996 : A group of African leaders agreed to impose full
economic sanctions on Burundi after a Tutsi military coup and called for international support.
